answer.evidence: The object is a tall flat signboard drawn face-on. The width stays at 14 px from row 1 to row 30, with no widening or narrowing that would form an ellipse. Rows 1-5 are a white header plate with a slightly darker last row (row 5), then a dark outline at row 6. I read this as a vertical blank title plate, not a horizontal top surface: it is flat-shaded, has no eave shadow, and sits directly above the red face. The red board (rows 7-27) and the grey base strip (rows 28-30) are also vertical faces. No row shows a receding horizontal top or a side face, so it is a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow standing sign with a dark red face, a light frame and white hangul. The measured facts put it at 10 visible tones per tile, between bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12), and below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, below bus-shelter-a's 9% and equal to kiosk-a and vending-a. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark red-brown rather than a black sticker line, which matches the references. By eye, the red face has a few steps of shading, the frame has highlight and shadow edges, and the lettering adds detail. It is a simple single-purpose prop, and a careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking thinner or flatter than the bus shelter or kiosk. It has fewer ramp steps than vending-a, but that is acceptable for a sign this small.
